arguments.summary: Decision: assess differentiated 21/63-session research theses for ANET, QQQ, MU, META and NVDA versus declared SPY and sector benchmarks; do not force rankings, forecasts or allocations. Grouped neutral assignments were accepted for company fundamentals/valuation, macro, technicals and geopolitics. Commodities is omitted at planning because no direct commodity-price source or clearly material commodity transmission has been established; semiconductor supply-chain risk is covered by geopolitics/company work.

claims.text: Research assignments to Company, Macro, Technical and Geopolitics were accepted for the full relevant watchlist scope.

A defensible 21/63-session assessment requires reconciling issuer fundamentals, QQQ holdings look-through, macro/rates, price behavior and geopolitical policy channels; no single channel is presumed decisive at planning.

gaps.description: No completed specialist evidence is available yet for issuer fundamentals, ETF holdings look-through, macro, technicals or geopolitical channels; instrument assessments are therefore premature.

assumptions: SPY and stated XLK/XLC comparisons are fixed contextual benchmarks, not allocation recommendations.
Company valuation sensitivities, if produced, will use explicit scenario EPS and P/E assumptions rather than consensus or calibrated forecasts.
arguments.counter_thesis: Near-term price behavior may be dominated by broad market/rates conditions or policy news rather than differentiated issuer catalysts, making company-specific scenario work insufficient on its own.

review_conditions.description: Review the integrated evidence after the four accepted specialist tasks complete; assess whether any common macro, technical or policy dependency overrides issuer-specific evidence.
